title: PoEM: Predicting New RL Outcomes from Existing Policies
claim: Policies trained on different rewards span a low-dimensional space, so a new reward's policy can be composed from them without retraining.
layout: 2 panels, left geometric then right left-to-right pipeline, numbered steps
description: Two panels side by side. Panel (a), "Low-rank structure in log-policy space", has a small legend at top left mapping colored rewards r1..rk through RL to expert policies π1..πk, with a mini diagram of near-orthogonal parameter-update arrows. Below it is a light-blue tilted plane. Colored arrows run from log π_ref to points log π1..log πk, labeled φ1..φk. A pink dot above the plane marks the target RL policy, and a purple arrow points to the predicted PoEM policy near it. Panel (b), "Recover weights from basis models", shows policies and calibration samples feeding a matrix of log-ratio squares. The matrix times α approximates the target scores t. Numbered steps (evaluate, fit linear regression, compose) lead to a purple recovered-weights box and a PoEM policy formula box. The eye goes first to the purple arrow in the plane, then to the purple box at lower right.
caption: Overview of \ours. (a) Policies $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_k$ post-trained with RL from a shared reference policy $\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ on different rewards have nearly orthogonal parameter updates, yet their policy log-ratios $\phi_k=\log\pi_k-\log\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}$ span a low-dimensional space. The RL outcome $\pi^*_{\mathrm{tar}}$ on a target reward can lie close to this space even when that reward is not a combination of the basis rewards, so a composition $\pi_{\methodm}$ of the basis approximates it. (b) \ours evaluates the basis log-ratios on shared calibration samples $(x,y)$, centers them within each prompt, and fits weights $\hat{\bm{\alpha}}$ by least squares to predict the centered scores of the target reward $r_{\mathrm{tar}}$ on the same samples. The \ours policy $\pi_{\methodm}$ composes the basis with these weights at inference time, with no new RL training.
abstract: Foundation models are post-trained with reinforcement learning (RL) to maximize specific rewards, such as helpfulness, correctness, or instruction following. This post-training process is computationally intensive, sometimes unstable, and has to be run from scratch every time the reward model changes or when we want to combine multiple rewards. We hence ask: given a new reward function, is it possible to predict the policy RL would produce without actually training on that reward? We answer this in the affirmative by introducing PoEM, a framework for predicting RL outcomes using models previously trained on other rewards. First, we build on the fact that if the new reward function can be written as a linear combination of existing ones, then the optimal policy can be expressed as a combination of the existing policies in log-probability space. Surprisingly, even in cases where the rewards are not linearly connected, we observe that policies learned through RL often span an approximately low-rank subspace across rewards. To our benefit, the weights for this combination can be estimated using only the reward or basis policy outputs on the samples. We turn these observations into an algorithm that takes post-trained models and a target reward function, and approximates the target RL policy without any additional RL training. We experimentally evaluate our approach across programmatic and learned rewards for open-ended generation, with additional experiments on math reasoning, tool calling, and image generation.
